title: Keto Peppermint Mocha Cupcakes
shortDescription: Rich keto coffee cupcakes with cocoa and sugar-free peppermint buttercream, ready in about 43 minutes total.
description: These cupcakes came out of my holiday baking week when I wanted a coffee shop treat without the sugar crash. I tested this batch three times to get the almond flour crumb soft, not gritty.
ingredients: 1/2 cup granular erythritol or monk fruit blend
1/2 cup unsalted butter, melted and cooled
2 sugar-free chocolate bars, chopped, for garnish
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk almond flour, cocoa powder, granular sweetener, espresso powder, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
In another bowl, beat eggs, melted butter, brewed coffee, and vanilla until smooth.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Stir just until combined, no dry streaks.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two-thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
Let cupcakes cool completely before frosting, about 30 minutes.
Beat cream cheese until smooth. Add powdered erythritol and peppermint extract, mix well.
In a separate bowl, whip heavy cream to stiff peaks. Fold into the cream cheese mix gently.
Pipe frosting high on each cooled cupcake. Top with chopped sugar-free chocolate.
tips: Use finely ground almond flour, not almond meal, for a smoother crumb.
Chill the frosting bowl and beaters before whipping cream. It holds shape better.
Add peppermint extract slowly and taste as you go. It gets strong fast.
Store cupcakes in the fridge in an airtight container. They keep for 4 days.

faq.question: Can I use sugar-free peppermint candy canes as garnish?
faq.answer: Check the label first. Most candy canes contain real sugar, which breaks the keto count. Look for a sugar-free version sweetened with isomalt or erythritol, or skip it and use crushed sugar-free chocolate instead.

faq.question: Why did my cupcakes sink in the middle?
faq.answer: This usually means the oven was too hot or the batter was overmixed. Stick to 325°F and stir just until the dry streaks disappear.

faq.question: Can I make these ahead for a holiday party?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store unfrosted in an airtight container. Whip the frosting fresh the day you serve them for the best texture.

faq.question: Is the coffee flavor strong or subtle?
faq.answer: It is a solid mocha flavor, not overpowering. The espresso powder in the batter and the coffee liquid work together, but the cocoa balances it out.

conclusion: These cupcakes bring coffee shop flavor to your holiday table without the sugar spike. Make a batch ahead and just whip the frosting fresh before your party.
